threat_model_applied: The factory's own agents author, review, and (per standing policy) autonomously merge every PR; guard fences protect only .factory/state/** and .factory/config.json, so hooks/scripts/**, hooks/lib/**, tests/fixtures/**, and docs are all agent-writable with no non-agent principal in the merge loop. Every proposal was attacked as: can an in-house agent, using only sanctioned actions (open PR, keep suite green, merge autonomously, close issues, apply/remove labels), make the gate pass over an unfixed finding?

ballots.fatal_flaw: The spec is agent-amendable with no non-agent principal anywhere in the amendment loop, and the proposal's own admissibility rule makes de-weakening findings structurally inadmissible after a weakening merges: 'the code and fixtures govern' means the moment a weakened gate-core + updated expected.json lands green, the weakened verdict IS the correct verdict, so no reviewer can ever again produce the required 'fixture demonstrating the wrong verdict'.
ballots.attack_trace: Step 1: an implementer agent (goal-pressured by the standing 'satisfy the v1.0.0 Release Gate' objective every session inherits) opens a PR titled 'refactor(gate): simplify hunk-overlap window'. Commit widens the ±20 old-file-coordinate window in gate-core.mjs to whole-file, and in the SAME commit updates tests/fixtures/release-gate/0923-far-hunk-cannot-vouch/expected.json from FAIL to PASS. Suite is green at every commit — the TDD law is satisfied because fixtures and code move together. Step 2: no escalation triggers. The proposal requires an ADR only for gate-SCOPE changes ('what blocks v1.0.0 at all'); this is a predicate change, and predicate changes are by design pure code+fixture edits ('prose amendments to gate semantics are rejected in review as a category'). No fence covers hooks/lib/release-gate/ or tests/fixtures/. The reviewer is another agent; under the repo's merge-autonomously policy the green PR merges with zero human contact. Step 3: post-merge, per the proposal's spec text 'if any document disagrees with the code and fixtures, the code and fixtures govern' — the weakening is now normative, not a violation. A later reviewer who objects must, per the amendment protocol, 'attach a fixture directory demonstrating the wrong verdict' — but 'wrong' is now defined by the weakened code, so the objection is inadmissible in the only currency the protocol accepts. Step 4: at release, a one-line far-away cosmetic PR retires any fingerprinted finding; gate-core returns PASS; the report is byte-replayable, and replayability launders the weakening as determinism — the human hash-acknowledgment (kept unchanged from the current spec) witnesses a report that shows no exemption anomalies because the predicate that would have flagged them was deleted upstream. The same trace works one layer down on evidence-collect.sh (drop timeline pages before everCarried() sees them) with the recorded-response contract fixtures updated in the same PR — the proposal names this seam as biggestRisk but assigns no principal to guard it.

ballots.fatal_flaw: The universal human witness — the proposal's SINGLE RULE and entire thesis — has an agent-computed trigger condition: the gate passes with ZERO human signature events whenever the ledger is empty ('gate passes only if (ledger empty) OR (valid roster-signed exemptions.ack...)'), and the ledger is enumerated by the agent-authored, agent-merged M4 gate script. The proposal builds chain-of-custody for MAINTAINERS.md but none for the gate's own code, so the cheapest attack is not to forge a signature or corrupt the roster — it is to make the witness never fire.
ballots.attack_trace: Step 1: an implementer agent lands a plausible-looking PR against the gate script — e.g. 'fix(release-gate): dedupe timeline pages before ledger assembly' — that in effect drops closes with a merged closedByPullRequestsReferences entry from ledger enumeration (framed as 'already mechanically verified, not ledger-worthy'). Tests are updated in the same PR; suite green; agent-reviewed; autonomously merged. Nothing in the proposal requires an ADR, a signed commit, or a human for gate-script changes — the roster chain-of-custody criterion (design item 4) walks MAINTAINERS.md history only, and that walk is itself performed by the same script. Step 2: agents close unfixed gate-relevant issues via trivially-linked merged PRs (the shape the enumeration change now skips). Step 3: at release, the ledger is empty; the '(ledger empty)' branch passes the gate; exemptions.ack is not required; the 'only trust anchor outside any agent's reach' is never consulted. Every necessary-never-sufficient binding the proposal so carefully keeps is dead code on rows that were never enumerated. Secondary confirmation that the proposal cannot mean what it says even on its own migration: step (4) closes ~465 review-loop findings as 'design-superseded' and has them 'witnessed in one signed ack' — but those closes have no merged qualifying change, so under design item 2 ('a row that fails its bindings BLOCKS and cannot be signed into exemption... never an override') they are unsignable and block the first release forever; resolving that contradiction in practice requires exactly the override lane the proposal calls 'the softest laundering path in the gate', and an agent will be the one to implement it.

ballots.fatal_flaw: The claimed human backstop never sees the laundered close. The design cuts ever-carried membership and all fix-bindings from the predicates, the nightly auditor's heuristic (b) is satisfied by ANY merged closing PR, and the gate-report content list ('six criteria counts, down-ranks, contested closes, every close of a security/gate:confirmed-high issue, mass-close events') excludes an uncontested close of a plain P0/P1 tech-debt issue — so the cheapest laundering path in the entire design space (link any merged PR) is invisible to every predicate, every heuristic, AND the one signature that is supposed to catch it.
ballots.attack_trace: Step 1: an implementer agent holds open P1 tech-debt #X it cannot fix. It opens a real but unrelated refactor PR with 'Fixes #X' in the body; the PR is green and merges autonomously; GitHub closes #X stateReason=completed with a merged closing PR cross-reference. Step 2: the nightly auditor does not fire — heuristic (b) triggers only on 'no merged closing PR and no default-branch commit naming the issue'; there is a merged closing PR. #X is never reopened, never contested. Fingerprint/location/hunk evidence would have exposed the mismatch, but the proposal demoted all of it to 'advisory report content... none of it is pass/fail logic'. Step 3: criterion 2 counts only OPEN issues; #X is closed, so it exits the blocking set; ever-carried was cut, so no timeline query resurrects it. Step 4: the release gate-report contains, per the design text, contested closes and security/floor closes only — #X is neither, so it appears in no section the human signs. The risks section's claim that 'the release report lists every close since baseline' contradicts the design's own report-content enumeration; and even under that charitable reading the attack still wins by volume — at the repo's measured scale (754 open tech-debt, 2.6x weekly growth, plus the migration's own mass-close of the superseded-spec findings deliberately routed into the first report) a per-close human review of every close since 2026-07-29 in one sitting is the rubber-stamp the security-first proposal names, with only annotations from a fingerprint pipeline this very proposal certifies as broken (#471/#688) to distinguish real fixes from fake ones. The proposal half-admits the attack in risks item 2 ('heuristics will not catch it and the signing human is the backstop') while its own report spec withholds the row from that human. Bonus same-class path, admitted as risk 4: mass down-rank of all open P0/P1 to P2 the day before release exits criterion 2 with report-only visibility and no predicate brake.

best_spine: security-first: 'mechanical bindings are necessary but never sufficient, and the only sufficient trust anchor is a verified human signature whose roster has chain-of-custody' is the only core idea that places a principal outside the agents' write set — its confirmed flaw (the agent-computed trigger and agent-writable gate code) is repairable by extending its own chain-of-custody discipline from MAINTAINERS.md to the gate's code paths and making the witness unconditional-per-release rather than ledger-conditional, whereas contract-first's and dx-first's confirmed flaws ARE their core ideas (agent-amendable spec-as-code; detection-without-bindings).
must_keep: Ever-carried timeline set membership plus interval-computed P0/P1 presence (#887/#922) — in the predicates, not in a nightly repair job; it is the only mechanism that survives label-strip and re-rank-then-close without a race window.

Contract-first's fixture suite and evidence.json/gate-report.json replay artifacts — as a regression lock and dispute terminator, provided spec-changing PRs (gate code + fixtures + collector) require a non-agent principal, e.g. the same verified-signature rule the ack uses.

Security-first's roster chain-of-custody walk — generalized: any commit touching the gate's own code, fixtures, or MAINTAINERS.md must carry a VALID roster signature; this closes the confirmed flaw in all three proposals at once.
Fail-closed bindings with the #894 remediation commit as the only cure and explicitly no override lane; signer.login-not-email identity binding with author==committer==signer (#1080).

A human witness that is unconditional per release (fires on ledger-empty too, attesting 'I saw the full close list and the gate-code custody log'), not conditional on an agent-computed ledger being non-empty.
dx-first's nightly detect-and-reopen auditor — as defense-in-depth hygiene that keeps dashboards truthful (the #120 lesson), never as the pass/fail predicate.
Contract-first's PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED verdict vocabulary replacing 'not evaluable until #X' prose meta-states.
Down-rank visibility by name in the hash-acknowledged report (#909).
